column1: # OWASP ZAP rules for scripts/ci/zap/run-zap.sh (baseline + API scans).
# Reviewed 2026-11-16 against the first full scan of 0.10.0-dev.
# Policy: every alert ZAP raises fails the run (scripts/ci/zap/gate.mjs),
# unless this file ignores or accepts it, and every such line says why.
# Nothing here hides a finding that was real: those were fixed in the code
# (see test/dast-regressions.e2e-spec.ts).
# Formats (fields are TAB-separated):
#   <plugin id>  IGNORE      <reason>        whole plugin; ZAP syntax
#   <plugin id>  OUTOFSCOPE  <url regex>     plugin on matching URLs; ZAP syntax
#   #@accept  <alertRef>  <url regex>  <reason>  [exact evidence]
#       one alert on matching URLs, optionally requiring exact evidence;
#       read only by gate.mjs (ZAP skips comment lines)
# ── Informational rules: they describe the application, not a weakness ──
# "A login form / session cookie was identified": ZAP's own bookkeeping.

column3: Authentication Request Identified (informational: ZAP found the login form)
Session Management Response Identified (informational: ZAP found the session cookie)
Modern Web Application (informational: the page uses JavaScript)

column1: # Escaped by Handlebars ({{...}} HTML-escapes): the OAuth parameters reflected
# into hidden inputs cannot break out of the attribute. Covered by
# test/dast-regressions.e2e-spec.ts ("reflected OAuth parameters").
# The User Agent Fuzzer only reports that responses differ by User-Agent.

column3: User Agent Fuzzer (informational: lists responses that vary by User-Agent)
User Controllable HTML Element Attribute (informational; values are HTML-escaped)

column1: # ── Accepted per alert, with the reason ──
# Cache classification. Non-storable is the desired state for dynamic
# responses (they are no-store since this review).
#@accept
column4: Non-Storable Content is what dynamic responses should be: they are sent with Cache-Control: no-store.

column1: # Static theme CSS and public OIDC metadata are meant to be cached.
#@accept
column4: Theme stylesheets are static, public and versioned with the image; caching them is intended.

column1: #@accept
column4: Static theme assets and public OIDC metadata (discovery, JWKS) are public and meant to be cached by clients.

column1: # 4xx responses to fuzzed input are correct behaviour. 5xx (100000-2) stay
# a failure except the documented upstream failure and upgrade endpoints below.
#@accept
column4: A 4xx answer to fuzzed or invalid input is the correct response, not a weakness.

column1: # The wizard now really sends mail. Fuzzed SMTP settings have no reachable
# mail server in this scan, so 502 is expected. Other statuses still fail.
#@accept
column4: SMTP delivery failure is a documented 502 when the scanner's saved mail server is unreachable; unexpected 500/503 responses remain failures.

column1: # The upgrade API answers 503 by design while UPGRADE_API_ENABLED is unset
# (docs/docs/deployment/upgrading.mdx); the scan runs with it unset.
# The same 503 makes ZAP see a generic error body there (production hides
# 5xx details); also by design, and only on these two paths.
# Hosted pages (login, consent, account, device, broker callback) are HTML
# endpoints that also appear in the OpenAPI document, so the API scan
# expected JSON from them.
#@accept
column4: Browser-facing endpoints (including the SAML broker's start, ACS and complete pages) return HTML, SAML metadata is XML, and theme assets return CSS/images, by design; the scanner expected JSON from them.

column1: # CSP form-action is deliberately absent on hosted pages: Chrome applies it
# to the redirect after a form POST, so the login form's 302 to the client's
# redirect_uri (another origin) would be blocked and sign-in would break.
# Documented in buildThemeCsp (src/theme/theme-render.service.ts); every
# other directive without a fallback is set (frame-ancestors, base-uri,
# object-src via default-src). The admin console's CSP does set form-action.
#@accept
column4: Hosted pages omit form-action by design: Chrome enforces it on the post-login redirect to the client's redirect_uri, which would break sign-in (see buildThemeCsp).

column1: # COEP is for cross-origin isolation (SharedArrayBuffer, precise timers),
# which no Idenplane page uses; require-corp/credentialless would block the
# CAPTCHA providers' iframes on the registration page. COOP (same-origin)
# and CORP (same-origin, cross-origin only for /themes/) are set.
#@accept
column4: COEP only enables cross-origin isolation, which Idenplane does not use; it would break third-party CAPTCHA iframes. COOP and CORP are set.

column1: # ── False positives ──
# The token and device endpoints answer an unauthenticated client with
# WWW-Authenticate: Basic, as RFC 6749 section 5.2 requires. ZAP flags Basic
# because the CI scan talks plain HTTP inside a private Docker network; in
# production these endpoints are served over TLS (BASE_URL is https).
#@accept
column4: RFC 6749 5.2 challenge; flagged only because the CI scan uses plain HTTP on a private network. Production serves these over TLS.

column1: # The "private IP" is the scanner's own input echoed back: the OpenAPI
# example for a device certificate's SAN (src/nhi/dto/certificate.dto.ts,
# 'DNS:device.internal,IP:192.168.1.100').
#@accept
column4: The address is the OpenAPI example value the scanner submitted (certificate.dto.ts), echoed back; no server address is disclosed.

column1: # Prometheus exposition format includes process start times; the endpoint
# is admin-authenticated.
#@accept
column4: Prometheus metrics carry process timestamps by design; the endpoint requires admin authentication.

column1: # Parameter NAMES such as userId/includeUsers and an e-mail search filter on
# admin-only search endpoints: identifiers, not secrets, sent to the admin API.
#@accept
column4: Admin search filters (userId, email, includeUsers) are identifiers sent to an authenticated admin API, not credentials.

column1: # Magic links are e-mailed URLs, so their token has to be in the URL. It is
# single-use and short-lived, and the verify page is no-store.
#@accept
column4: A magic link is an e-mailed URL, so its single-use, short-lived token must be in the query string.

column1: # Stored values containing <script> come back inside JSON from the admin API.
# Responses are application/json with X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, so a
# browser never renders them; the admin console renders through React, which
# escapes text. ZAP itself rates this LOW confidence for non-HTML responses.
#@accept
column4: Stored input echoed in application/json (nosniff) admin API responses is not executable; the console renders it escaped.

column1: # Boolean SQL injection on step-up/challenge: a false positive. `acr` is only
# compared with constants and passed to Prisma as a bound parameter (no raw
# SQL anywhere in src/step-up); without a session cookie, as in the scan,
# every value gets the same 400 and the "difference" ZAP saw is the
# timestamp and rate limiting of repeated requests.
# The public registration-fields list returns the labels an admin configured,
# as application/json with nosniff. The hosted register page renders them
# with Handlebars' escaping {{displayName}}, never {{{ }}}.
#@accept
column4: Admin-configured field labels echoed in an application/json (nosniff) response; the register page renders them HTML-escaped.

column1: #@accept
column4: False positive: acr is only compared with constants and bound by Prisma; no raw SQL in src/step-up, and the unauthenticated scan always gets the same 400.

column1: # Registration: the boolean pair (John AND 1=1 -- / John AND 1=2 --) is sent as
# two registrations of the same form; the first creates the user and the
# second is refused as a duplicate, so the pages differ. src/registration
# has no raw SQL; every value is bound by Prisma.
#@accept
column4: False positive: the second of the paired registrations is a duplicate of the first, so the responses differ; registration uses only Prisma-bound queries (no raw SQL in src/registration).

column1: # ZAP 90035 can find the computed number inside a DIFFERENT unevaluated
# Django-addition probe in the same realm export. The gate's special matcher
# requires that exact collision, the original input unchanged, and no computed
# result outside literal probes. Missing proof or an evaluated result still fails.
# Regression: test/dast-regressions.e2e-spec.ts and stored-ssti-collision.test.mjs.
#@accept
column4: False positive only when ZAP's alleged result occurs exclusively inside other unevaluated stored addition probes in the same realm export.
